title: Choose how recipes are arranged
question: Each layout keeps routing, timing and edits distinct. Choose the structure that makes a reusable release sequence easiest to understand.

options.label: Release outline
options.thesis: A clear sequence on the left, focused editing in the middle, and the recipe outcome always visible.
options.viewport: Source trigger above an indexed release list; the selected release opens beside it with destination, timing and description controls.
options.risk: Focuses on one release at a time; comparing detailed descriptions requires switching releases.

raised.raise: Every release retains a readable place and publication reference.
Source and treatment context stay registered while settings change.
The selected release carries the strongest emphasis; supporting details recede.

options.label: Studio sheet
options.thesis: Keep the whole recipe in one column, expanding only the release being edited.
options.viewport: Compact source strip, vertically connected release rows, one expanded form and a persistent save bar.
options.risk: Familiar and efficient; closer to a conventional workflow editor than a distinct workspace.

options.label: Schedule lanes
options.thesis: Lead with when each release happens, then edit its content in a dedicated panel.
options.viewport: Source on the left, release timing across the work area, selected release settings below and save at the edge.
options.case: Stronger time comparison, but less direct than an outline for everyday recipe editing.
options.risk: An unfamiliar schedule rule can make the time-led overview less useful.

options.label: Data field
options.thesis: A working-screen translation of data field.
options.viewport: Product shell with source, release editing and save areas.
options.risk: Its source vocabulary competes with the familiar task.
options.case: Strong scan hierarchy, but the numeric/barcode vocabulary does not help artists publish.

options.label: Star atlas
options.thesis: A working-screen translation of star atlas.
options.viewport: Product shell with source, release editing and save areas.
options.risk: Its source vocabulary competes with the familiar task.
options.case: Artistic association is strong; coordinate navigation adds interpretation to a routine task.
options.kept: Clear emphasis for the selected release.

options.label: Guide map
options.thesis: A working-screen translation of guide map.
options.viewport: Product shell with source, release editing and save areas.
options.risk: Its source vocabulary competes with the familiar task.
options.case: Playful organic regions conflict with the requested restrained working screen.
options.kept: Distinct functional regions without extra headings.

options.label: Seasonal folio
options.thesis: A working-screen translation of seasonal folio.
options.viewport: Product shell with source, release editing and save areas.
options.risk: Its source vocabulary competes with the familiar task.
options.case: Transformation comparison transfers well; seasonal navigation does not fit posting rules.

options.label: Design annual
options.thesis: A working-screen translation of design annual.
options.viewport: Product shell with source, release editing and save areas.
options.risk: Its source vocabulary competes with the familiar task.
options.case: The attribution-led composition gives secondary metadata too much authority.
options.kept: Consistent alignment between content and metadata.

canonCard.label: Compact workflow table
canonCard.thesis: Keep all releases in a familiar, carefully spaced table with inline editors.
canonCard.viewport: Source above destination, schedule and modification columns, with contextual sections below each row.
canonCard.risk: Fast to scan, but repeating complex descriptions can recreate the current hierarchy problem.
